title: Representatives and eventual zero for a tensor base-change diagram
statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preorder, $B:I	o\mathrm{CommRing}$ and $\kappa_i:B_i	o S$ a ring colimit cocone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $M$ be an $S$-module, $D:I	o\mathrm{Ab}$ a diagram with $B_i$-module structures, and $
u_i:D_i	o M$ an additive cocone with $
u_i(yx)=\kappa_i(y)
u_i(x)$. Suppose the maps $B_j\otimes_{B_i}D_i	o D_j$, $y\otimes x\mapsto yD(i	o j)(x)$ for $i\le j$, and $S\otimes_{B_i}D_i	o M$, $y\otimes x\mapsto y
u_i(x)$, are linear isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then every $x\in M$ is $
u_i(y)$ for some $i,y$, and every $x\in D_i$ with $
u_i(x)=0$ maps to zero in some $D_j$ with $j\ge i$. No finite-generation or finite-presentation assumption is needed, and the index universe and group universe may be unrelated.

source.place: Algebra, Tags 00D6, 00D7 and 00DD, elementwise tensor-colimit argument used for Tag 00QX

proof.text: For any fixed i₀ take the upper tail. Regard the stage rings there and S as B(i₀)-modules via the given ring maps. Build the linear map from their module direct limit to S. Ring-colimit representatives show surjectivity, after moving a stage to the tail. Ring-colimit eventual equality shows injectivity, hence this map is a linear equivalence.
Tensor this equivalence with D(i₀) and compose with the inverse of TensorProduct.directLimitLeft. Tensor induction checks that its value on a stage tensor is the map κ_i tensor id.

For a stage i above i₀, choose the assumed equivalence B_i tensor D(i₀) to D_i. Tensor induction and cocone naturality prove that its composite with ν_i equals the S tensor comparison after κ_i tensor id. Represent the inverse image of x under the S equivalence in the tensor direct limit and apply the stage equivalence, obtaining a representative of x.

For x in D(i₀) with ν_i₀(x)=0 take 1 tensor x at the least tail index. The S comparison sends it to zero; its injectivity and the tensor-colimit equivalence imply its direct-limit class is zero. Module.DirectLimit.of.zero_exact gives a later vanishing tensor. The later-stage equivalence carries it to D(i₀ → j)(x).
